corridor.description: French nationals are EEA citizens and benefit from the EU/EEA free movement of persons agreement with Norway (EEA Agreement, Annex V). No prior work permit is required. The employee may start work immediately on arrival and must register with the Norwegian police (Politiet) within 3 months if intending to stay more than 3 months. Norway is not an EU member but is part of the EEA, so EU free movement rules apply.

primary_sources.title: Registration for EEA/EU nationals — Norwegian Directorate of Immigration (UDI)
Working in Norway — Norwegian Tax Administration (Skatteetaten)
NOKUT — Norwegian Agency for Quality Assurance in Education
Police registration for EU/EEA nationals — Politiet

pathways.duration_basis: Indefinite right of residence as long as conditions are met (employed, self-employed, or sufficient means + comprehensive sickness insurance).
Derived from the EEA primary resident's right of residence.

required_documents.document_name: EEA Free Movement pathway overview for France → Norway
required_documents.description: French nationals have an automatic right to reside and work in Norway under EEA free movement (EEA Agreement, Annex V). No prior visa or work permit is needed. If staying more than 3 months they must register with Norwegian police within that period.

required_documents.document_name: Family Reunification pathway overview for FR→NO
required_documents.description: Non-EEA family members of an EEA national residing in Norway may derive a right of residence. EEA family members (e.g., French spouse) have the same right of residence as the primary EEA national. Both must register with police.

France is an EU/EEA member state. Norway is an EEA (non-EU) member. The EEA Agreement grants French nationals the right to move freely to Norway for work, self-employment, study or family reasons without a visa or work permit. Classification: eea_to_eea free movement.

required_documents.document_name: Valid French passport or national identity card
Proof of employment in Norway (employment contract or employer letter)
Proof of accommodation / address in Norway (lease, utility bill, or employer-provided housing confirmation)
Police registration form for EEA nationals (submitted at local police station)
Signed employment contract with Norwegian employer
Employer attestation confirming employment (signed letter on company letterhead with salary and start date)
required_documents.condition_expression: required if employment contract is not yet signed

required_documents.document_name: Proof of family relationship with EEA national (marriage certificate, birth certificate, or dependency proof)
EEA registration eligibility conditions summary for FR→NO
required_documents.description: French nationals may register as EEA residents in Norway if: (a) employed or self-employed, OR (b) a student with sufficient means and comprehensive sickness insurance, OR (c) have sufficient means and comprehensive sickness insurance. No salary minimum applies. Registration certificate issued free of charge.

required_documents.document_name: EEA registration fee schedule for FR→NO
required_documents.description: Police registration for EEA nationals is free of charge (NOK 0). The registration certificate (bevis for registrering) is issued at the appointment. No stamp duty or processing fee applies for EU/EEA citizens registering under free movement rights.

required_documents.document_name: Jobseeker rights and residence period for EEA nationals in Norway
required_documents.description: French nationals may enter Norway to look for work without registration for up to 3 months. After 3 months, they must demonstrate genuine job-seeking activity and a reasonable chance of success to remain. The Directorate of Immigration (UDI) assesses this on request. If they find employment they must register within the standard 3-month window.

required_documents.document_name: Academic qualification recognition via NOKUT (Norwegian Agency for Quality Assurance in Education)
required_documents.condition_expression: required for regulated professions (physician, nurse, teacher, engineer with Norwegian licensing board requirements)

required_documents.document_name: EEA registration deadline: 3 months from arrival
required_documents.description: EEA nationals who intend to stay in Norway for more than 3 months must register with the Norwegian police (Politiet) before the end of that 3-month period. Failure to register is a minor offence but does not invalidate the right of residence derived from EEA membership. The 3-month period starts from the date of first entry into Norway.

post_arrival_steps.name: Register with Norwegian police (Politiet) — EEA registration certificate
post_arrival_steps.deadline_basis: EEA Agreement: registration required within 3 months of entry for stays exceeding 3 months.
post_arrival_steps.where: Local police station (politistasjon) — bring passport and employment proof

post_arrival_steps.name: Register address in Folkeregisteret (National Population Register)
post_arrival_steps.deadline_basis: Required within 14 days of establishing a Norwegian address (Folkeregisterloven §19).
post_arrival_steps.where: Tax Administration (Skatteetaten) office or online at skatteetaten.no

post_arrival_steps.name: Obtain Norwegian tax card (skattekort) from Skatteetaten
post_arrival_steps.deadline_basis: Required before first payroll run; employer withholds flat 25% tax without a skattekort.
post_arrival_steps.where: Online via skatteetaten.no or at local Skatteetaten office

post_arrival_steps.name: Apply for Norwegian D-number (temporary national identification number)
post_arrival_steps.deadline_basis: Required for banking, tax purposes, and most official interactions before a permanent Norwegian ID number is issued.
post_arrival_steps.where: Tax Administration (Skatteetaten) via employer or in person at Folkeregisteret

post_arrival_steps.name: Submit academic credential for NOKUT recognition (regulated professions only)
post_arrival_steps.condition_expression: required for regulated professions requiring Norwegian licensing

post_arrival_steps.name: Register accompanying family member (spouse/partner) with police
post_arrival_steps.deadline_basis: Same 3-month window as the EEA primary resident.
post_arrival_steps.where: Local police station — family member must attend in person

path_classifier_rules.rationale: French nationals are EEA citizens with an automatic right to work in Norway; no work permit required.
EEA family members derive residence rights from the primary EEA national.

known_gaps: Social security coordination (A1 certificate for posted workers) is not covered — handled separately.
Permanent residence (permanent oppholdstillatelse) after 5 years is out of scope.
Detailed process for regulated professions (healthcare, teaching) licensing beyond NOKUT recognition is not encoded.
